notes: Synthetic: authored from the OpenAI OpenAPI spec as published in github.com/openai/openai-python api_reference/openapi.transformed.yml and the types generated from it (src/openai/types/chat/chat_completion.py, chat_completion_chunk.py, completion_usage.py, shared/chat_model.py), commit 35fc9f3 of 2026-10-28; SSE framing and per-chunk field order follow the live-recorded stream snapshots in that repo (.inline-snapshot/external/*.bin, recorded from api.openai.com). platform.openai.com and developers.openai.com were not reachable from the authoring sandbox. GPT-5.6 is documented there as gpt-5.6-sol / -terra / -luna (ChatModel; no dated snapshot is listed, so the alias is the model ID). Pins what the spec documents as gpt-5.6-and-later: prompt_cache_options (PromptCacheOptionsParam: "Supported for gpt-5.6 and later models") and the cache_write_tokens counter it reports in usage.prompt_tokens_details, plus fast mode (service_tier "fast" in the request, "priority" in the response, per ServiceTier) and reasoning_effort "xhigh". custom_tool_call pins a GPT-5-family custom tool (ChatCompletionCustomToolParam in the request, ChatCompletionMessageCustomToolCall in the response, with custom.name and custom.input instead of function). Otherwise the Chat Completions response shape is the same as gpt-5.5's. stream_text also pins a request-side loss (known gap O5): the client's stream_options.include_obfuscation false is dropped (models.StreamOptions only has include_usage), so the upstream keeps sending obfuscation padding.

allowed_unknown_fields.reason: known gap O1: message.refusal is dropped (models.Message has no refusal field). A structured-outputs refusal arrives as content null plus a refusal string, so the client receives content null, no refusal and finish_reason "stop": an empty answer it cannot tell from a refusal. null in every case without a refusal

known gap O4: a custom tool call's payload (custom.name and custom.input) is dropped: models.ToolCall only has function, so the client receives a tool call of type "custom" with an empty name and empty arguments and cannot act on it. The request side forwards custom tools (models.Tool keeps their raw bytes), so this hits every client that uses them
known gap O2: delta.refusal is dropped (models.Delta has no refusal field), so a streamed refusal reaches the client as empty deltas. null on the first chunk of an ordinary stream

known gap O3: streamed choice logprobs are dropped (models.StreamChoice has no logprobs field), so a stream with logprobs: true carries none to the client; the non-stream path keeps them. null unless logprobs were requested
